candidates.environmentToExplore: A quiet setting with room to make visible drafts and try original approaches
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Choose one everyday object and make three deliberately different visual drafts with paper or a free drawing tool.
candidates.costNote: Paper and a pencil are sufficient; paid materials are optional.
candidates.safetyNote: Use non-toxic materials and ventilate the room if paints or sprays are added.
candidates.accessibilityNote: A seated paper, tablet, collage, or verbal-description version can use the same prompt.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A focused problem-solving setting with autonomy, clear feedback, and small testable outputs
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Use a browser playground to change one tiny program, predict the result, run it, and note what changed.
candidates.costNote: A free browser playground is enough; no course or paid software is required.
candidates.safetyNote: Do not paste secrets or personal data into an unfamiliar online playground.
candidates.accessibilityNote: Keyboard navigation, zoom, screen readers, or a paired navigator can support the experiment.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A calm inquiry setting where evidence can be compared before reaching a conclusion
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Pick one small question, compare two sources, and write one claim, one uncertainty, and one next question.
candidates.costNote: Use library, public-domain, or already available sources before buying materials.
candidates.safetyNote: For medical, legal, or financial questions, treat the note as learning rather than professional advice.
candidates.accessibilityNote: Text-to-speech, audio sources, large print, or dictation can replace dense reading and typing.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A predictable setting with visible order, repeatable steps, and incremental improvement
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Choose one drawer or recurring task, map its current steps, and test one reversible simplification.
candidates.costNote: Rearrange what is already available; containers or apps are optional.
candidates.safetyNote: Do not move medication, emergency equipment, or another person's belongings without agreement.
candidates.accessibilityNote: The experiment can be done from a seated position or as a verbal process map with a partner.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A hands-on setting that combines practical steps, creative variation, and an observable result
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Using ingredients already available, make or plan one simple variation and record what you changed and why.
candidates.costNote: Set a fixed ingredient cap and use pantry items before buying specialized tools.
candidates.safetyNote: Check allergies, food handling, heat, and knife safety; use a no-cook version if needed.
candidates.accessibilityNote: A seated station, pre-cut ingredients, adaptive utensils, or a no-cook planning version can reduce barriers.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A concrete, hands-on setting with visible cause-and-effect and careful quality checks
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Inspect one non-critical object, sketch how its parts connect, and identify one reversible maintenance step without dismantling it.
candidates.costNote: Observation and a maintenance checklist require no tool purchase.
candidates.safetyNote: Do not open electrical, pressurized, load-bearing, or safety-critical equipment; ask a qualified person instead.
candidates.accessibilityNote: Use photographs, magnification, tactile labels, or a partner description instead of handling small parts.

candidates.environmentToExplore: An observational outdoor setting with movement, changing details, and self-directed pacing
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Observe from one safe location and record five patterns in light, plants, weather, sound, or movement.
candidates.costNote: A window, balcony, courtyard, or nearby public space can replace paid travel or gear.
candidates.safetyNote: Stay on accessible public routes, check weather, and do not approach wildlife or unsafe terrain.
candidates.accessibilityNote: The observation can be stationary, window-based, audio-focused, or completed with a companion.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A flexible practice setting with body feedback, self-paced repetition, and room for expression
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Create a three-movement seated or standing sequence, repeat it slowly, and note comfort and energy before and after.
candidates.costNote: No equipment or subscription is needed.
candidates.safetyNote: Stay within a pain-free range, use stable support, and stop for dizziness, sharp pain, or breathing difficulty.
candidates.accessibilityNote: Every movement may be seated, reduced in range, imagined, or guided by a trusted partner.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A collaborative setting where understanding grows through listening, explanation, and feedback
candidates.experiment20Minutes: With consent, take turns explaining a familiar topic for five minutes and ask only clarifying questions before offering feedback.
candidates.costNote: Use a free call or an in-person conversation; no class purchase is needed.
candidates.safetyNote: Get consent, avoid confidential topics, and allow either person to stop without explanation.
candidates.accessibilityNote: Speech, chat, captions, asynchronous voice notes, or an AAC tool can all support the exchange.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A structured group setting with clear rules, turn-taking, coordination, and visible progress
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Facilitate one short cooperative puzzle or card round, explain the rules, and ask what made participation easier or harder.
candidates.costNote: Use cards, paper, or a free digital cooperative puzzle before buying a game.
candidates.safetyNote: Set respectful rules, avoid gambling stakes, and offer a no-pressure exit.
candidates.accessibilityNote: Use large-print cards, verbal descriptions, untimed turns, or a remote shared board.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A purpose-led setting that combines listening, coordination, and practical community impact
candidates.experiment20Minutes: List three needs visible in a community you know, then verify one by reading a public request from a credible local organization.
candidates.costNote: Research first; do not donate or buy supplies during the experiment.
candidates.safetyNote: Use public information, protect vulnerable people's privacy, and work through credible organizations.
candidates.accessibilityNote: The mapping can be remote, text-based, paced over breaks, or completed with a support person.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A decision-oriented setting with competing evidence, explicit trade-offs, and a concise recommendation
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Choose a reversible everyday decision and write the goal, two options, one argument for each, one risk, and a next check.
candidates.costNote: Use paper or a free note tool; do not buy decision templates.
candidates.safetyNote: Use a reversible low-stakes choice; medical, legal, financial, and employment decisions need qualified context.
candidates.accessibilityNote: Dictation, symbols, a verbal recording, or a partner scribe can replace writing.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A cross-cultural social setting with curiosity, mutual help, and rapid conversational feedback
candidates.experiment20Minutes: With a willing partner, exchange five useful phrases each and finish by checking which correction style felt comfortable.
candidates.costNote: Use a trusted partner or free exchange; paid tutoring is not required for the experiment.
candidates.safetyNote: Protect contact details, use platform safety tools, and leave disrespectful interactions.
candidates.accessibilityNote: Text chat, captions, slower pacing, AAC, or asynchronous messages are valid exchange modes.

candidates.environmentToExplore: A private, low-stimulation setting with autonomy and time to notice patterns before acting
candidates.experiment20Minutes: Describe one recent energizing moment, one draining moment, and one small environmental change to test this week.
candidates.costNote: Paper, an offline note, or a voice memo is sufficient.
candidates.safetyNote: Keep the prompt observational; pause and seek appropriate support if reflection becomes overwhelming.
candidates.accessibilityNote: Writing, drawing, voice recording, symbols, or silent reflection can all capture the experiment.
